challenges.says: The tradeoff admits the rule that the stamp can also be run by hand must still be offered, yet no step offers it, so the 'when someone runs it' half of businessrule-12414618955963878773 is silently dropped; and since the release workflow already stamps today, 'automate first' adds little beyond today.

This is today's script in new words (someone or the release asks, version is written) with a 'confirm what was stamped' step added, and that confirmation step honours the rule though it is a new behaviour; the variant is not a real alternative.

Rewording lost conditions: the language fallback drops 'unless the regional language is en-US' and the failure when the package has no en-US folder after files were already replaced (businessrule-24154317128059319852), the take-control step omits that it applies to whatever folder text is typed and ends the download with nothing moved (businessrule-16960626064100495277), and the result step loses that a failed final cleanup leaves files installed yet reports failure and no new folder (businessrule-17840470067823720423).

The step 'Install somewhere other than the usual folder' comes after the install has finished, so the person cannot choose a folder before it runs, and the person would also not be told that package is kept when extraction fails or that failures part-way leave some files replaced.

It only splits today's single dialog into labelled stages and keeps the choose-then-start shape, so it repeats today rather than offering another way; the splitting into 'prepare' and 'put in place' also blurs which failure message applies (take-control versus move, businessrule-70392920399990339776), and the replace-with-no-backup and cleanup-failure outcomes are not stated.

Step 'Come back to the definitions later' is marked new with the reason that today the text only says it can be done later, but today's Help | Acquire ADMX Files route already exists (businessrule-23603907625209300500), so the 'standing invitation' misstates the old system and duplicates the get-policy-definitions task; 'works out whether lacking without asking' is also exactly what happens today.

The tradeoff says a person who declines must find the later route themselves, but the offer text names Help | Acquire ADMX Files today; the variant just restates today's first-run dialog, and its steps drop that the message names that route.
